title: Example input for binary search
summary: The bar chart above and the array of cells below show the same sorted array and highlight the search target.
context: Given the strictly increasing sorted array nums = [1, 3, 6, 8, 12, 15, 23, 26, 31, 35], indexed from 0 to 9, find the target element target = 6.
description: The upper half of the figure, labeled “Represent the array as a bar chart,” arranges ten vertical bars of increasing height from left to right, with each element value shown above its bar and “Index” values from 0 to 9 labeled beneath the chart; the lower half shows the same array as ten contiguous horizontal cells. A double-headed arrow between the two halves indicates that the bar chart and the one-dimensional array are completely equivalent.

Element 6 at index 2 is highlighted in cyan in both the upper bar chart and the lower array cells: to its left are the smaller elements 1 and 3 at indices 0 and 1, and to its right are the larger elements 8, 12, 15, 23, 26, 31, and 35 at indices 3 through 9. This figure defines only the input data and search target without yet stepping through binary halving.

frames.title: Example input for binary search
frames.explanation: A successful search should return index 2, where the target is located.
